subject: dynamic indexing from JAGS to NIMBLE

messages.author: 5a5b99d05db5f9f4
messages.subject: dynamic indexing from JAGS to NIMBLE
parts:
Hi everyone,
I am in the process of converting a CJS mark-recapture model from JAGS to NIMBLE. 

In JAGS the following works but I get an error message in NIMBLE regarding dynamic indexing. I am not providing the entire model here - only the piece that resulted in error. I tried to provide the f vector as a constant but that didn't work.

Thanks in advance for any suggestions!

# After simulation compute vector with occasion of when host was first captured
f <- apply(sim$CH.sur, 1, get.first)  # outside NIMBLE model

# Estimate pathogen average on observed hosts
for(i in 1:N){ #in NIMBLE model
N.path.mean[i] <- mean(N.path.mean[i, f[i]:n.occasions])
}

ERROR message:
Dynamic indexing found in a vector of indices, f[i]:n.occasions. Only scalar indices, such as 'idx' in 'x[idx]', can be dynamic. One can instead use dynamic indexing in a vector of indices inside a nimbleFunction. To use constant indices, provide their values in `constants`.

messages.author: f116cbe5c604c988
messages.subject: Re: dynamic indexing from JAGS to NIMBLE
parts:
Maybe I'm looking at this too quickly, but this should work fine, so long as you provide f in the named constants list, which is provided as an argument to nimbleModel.  Is that what you did, when you said "I tried to provide the f vector as a constant but that didn't work"?

Skeleton code for providing f in the named constants list would look like:

constants <- list(f = f, ...)
...
model <- nimbleModel(..., constants = constants)

Cheers,
Daniel

messages.author: 7e75d660ca4eefd0
messages.subject: Re: dynamic indexing from JAGS to NIMBLE
parts:
Hi Andreas,

     There is more info your ERROR message described in section 5.1.2 of the NIMBLE manual.  See item 11 in the list describing how NIMBLE extends the bugs language.  

A nimbleFunction does allow dynamic indexing that yields a vector of indices, so you could set up a simple nimbleFunction to achieve your goal.  If your CJS model isn't modeling the latent alive/state, you could use the dCJSxx distributions from the nimbleEcology package.  I've modified these distributions to do just exactly what you intend above; that is, to allow releases of marked individuals at any occasion, not just the first.  Happy to share that if helpful.

Russ
